## 2b. Built to stand alone later (owner decision, 2026-10-10)
Cyrus stays a part of Nxeon for at least the next few months (to build a solid foundation and gather months of real Nxeon-customer usage data), then may become its own product. So:
- **Nothing breaks and nothing changes for customers:** same sign-in, same accounts, same wallet, same billing. No separate Cyrus login now.
- **Design for the split from day one (cheap now, expensive later):** Cyrus code reaches Nxeon only through a small **host seam** (sign-in/user, plan and billing, server access for install, storage, notifications). New code must not add new direct imports of Nxeon internals; where one is unavoidable it goes behind a named adapter. Cyrus tables stay Cyrus-prefixed with opaque ids for users/servers (no new foreign keys into Nxeon tables). The build service already stands alone; the engine core, asset pipelines, Test Flight and pack hosting already live under `lib/cyrus/` and stay game- and host-agnostic.
- **Later, when separating:** Nxeon implements the host side as an API (list servers, push plugin/pack/config, restart); a standalone Cyrus gets its own sign-in, wallet and billing, own database, and a standalone export (jar and pack download). The Kodely-to-Nxeon partner API is the existing pattern.
- **Not now:** no code that exists only to prepare the split beyond the seam rule and a coupling map.


### 4.7 Asset pipeline and studios
Shared studio core + per-game profile. Minecraft = pixel profile.
- **Texture** (top plan): LLM writes a pixel spec (palette + shapes), deterministic renderer draws it (raise the 400-op / 16-64 px limits for skins and larger atlases), optional pixel-model candidates later; per-mod **Style DNA** (palette ramps, outline rule, noise) for consistency; per-version validation; AI edits arrive as non-destructive candidates.
- **Sound** (Saka+): `SoundSpec` (events -> layers -> processing); tag the 514-file library by filename category; synthesis presets; processing in the browser from WAV, **server-side ffmpeg/libvorbis to mono Ogg Vorbis**; new namespaced sound keys played by the plugin (and silence the vanilla base mob; never override vanilla keys globally); mandatory subtitle keys. A complete mob set: ambient, hurt, death, step, attack, ability, spawn.
- **Models** (26.x first): `RigSpec` compiled by Nxeon code (3 archetypes, 5 procedural clips) to .bbmodel for **BetterModel** (MIT, pinned managed plugin). Handgun and similar items use static item models with display transforms, sounds and particles, no engine. Do not embed Blockbench (GPL app); do not depend on ModelEngine/FreeMinecraftModels/CraftEngine.
- **Quality bar**: rubric + metrics (texture palette size, contrast, edge density, banding, transparent policy; sound mono, true peak, loudness band per role, silence ratio) plus a vision-model judge calibrated on 100 owner-labelled samples; owner reviews a gallery.
- **Studios**: v1 minimal (miniPaint MIT stopgap or a small pixel editor; wavesurfer.js BSD waveform with trim/fade/layer and JSON edit recipes), then the full editors in R3. Library browsing follows the studio gate.

### 4.10 Per-game adapter contract (S, define in R0)
Artifact types and routes; toolchain profile and deny-list scan; version registry; knowledge pack; asset formats and **delivery** (Minecraft: server-pushed pack; Valheim: client zip; Terraria/Palworld: none; tModLoader: client mod); install rules; test lane; maturity level. Add `game` to every id and registry. Texture/Sound studios light up only where the adapter declares an asset format and delivery path. A realistic 3D/PBR profile is a later track; build only the interfaces now.

### R1b Full Texture and Sound Studios (owner priority, added 2026-10-10; Opus for the editor cores)
Moved forward from R3: the studios are a top priority, so the full editors come right after the first asset slice and before composition.
- **Texture Studio (top plan):** full pixel editor (layers, undo/redo, palettes and ramps, selection, tiling and 3D item preview, onion-skin for animated textures), library browsing and search, Style DNA applied across a whole mod, AI edits as non-destructive candidates with before/after diffs, reference-image-to-spec through a vision model, asset history, the quality rubric as a real review screen.
- **Sound Studio (Saka and up):** full waveform editor (zoom, regions, trim, fade, gain, pitch/time, layering, spectrum, loudness and true-peak readouts), library browsing and search by tag, synthesis presets, per-event mob/item sound sets, subtitle keys, non-destructive edit recipes, server-side Ogg export, asset history with waveform diffs.
- **Both:** shared studio core with per-game profiles (Minecraft pixel profile first); plan-tier gates enforced server-side; library follows the studio gate.
- **Done when:** a customer builds a complete set (e.g. banshee skin plus attack/hurt/death sounds) entirely in the studios without touching a prompt, and a real client shows and plays it (T).
- R3 keeps only animated creatures, gameplay designers and playtest scripts.

### Item model states and display contexts (owner question, 2026-10-10; queued after Studio UI part 1)
Today the pack builder emits ONE flat model per texture (handheld parent): one look, no states. Owner needs: how an item looks dropped, in an inventory slot, in first-person and third-person hand, on the head, in an item frame; and stateful items (a bow idle vs pulled back; a gun aiming/reloading).
- **ItemModelSpec v1** (new, in the asset spec): per-context display transforms (gui, ground, fixed/item frame, first/third person right+left hand, head) with per-category defaults (sword, tool, bow, gun, wand, shield) the owner/studio can override; named STATES each with a model/texture and the condition that selects it.
- **Mechanism (1.21.4+ item model definitions; names UNVERIFIED, must be checked against the docs and real servers before building):** `condition` on using_item, `range_dispatch` on use_duration/pull for pull stages, `select` on display_context, and plugin-set custom_model_data flags/strings (e.g. reloading, aiming); a custom bow is built on real bow behaviour with our item_model; a custom gun uses a consumable-style 'using' state for aiming and plugin flags for reload/cooldown. Limits: no free-form animation (texture frame animation via .mcmeta and fast model switching only; no real recoil). 1.21.1 needs the legacy predicate/custom-model-data overrides path (later).
- **Generator:** emits items/<name>.json (definition with conditions/range/select), one model JSON per state with its display block, and tests with golden hashes; the build prompt tells the plugin which states exist and the flag keys; registry capability checked per version.
- **Studio:** context switcher (hotbar, dropped, first-person, third-person, item frame, head) and a STATE scrubber (idle, pull 1-3, aim, reload) in the preview; correct 'in hand' placement (the grip in the hand: the first fix already requested of the Studio UI agent).
- **Later:** true 3D cuboid item models (the model pipeline) for guns/bows that should not be extruded sprites.

### Asset Library (owner requirement, 2026-10-10): one proper, cataloged, searchable library for sounds AND textures
The owner wants every asset cataloged and organized, not just filename-tagged. Shared design for both libraries:
- **Taxonomy as data** (committed JSON, not code): primary category, multi-valued **use cases** (where a mod uses it), free tags, descriptors derived from measured data (sound: duration class, intensity, pitch band, loopable heuristic, channels; texture: size, palette ramp, transparency, tileable, style), synonym table, and a licence/provenance ledger per asset (never asserting originality that has not been documented).
- **Sound categories:** Weapons (gunshot, reload, cocking, ricochet, melee swing, clash, bow), Creatures & Voices, Impacts & Destruction, Movement, Environment & Ambience, Doors & Mechanisms, UI & Alerts, Crowd & Reactions. **Use cases:** weapon_fire, weapon_reload, weapon_impact, melee, mob_ambient/hurt/death/attack/step, ability_cast, magic, boss_event, ui_notification, pickup_reward, block_interaction, door_mechanism, ambience_world, weather, explosion (gunshot + reload are both also tagged `weapon`).
- **Texture categories:** Items (weapon, tool, armor, food, potion, misc), Blocks (stone, wood, ore, plant, glass, decorative), Entity skins (humanoid, quadruped, flyer, ghost), GUI (button, panel, icon, HUD piece), Particles, and **Style DNA presets** (palette ramps, outline rule, noise level); sources: Cyrus-authored original template specs, the customer's uploads, textures from the customer's own projects, later community-shared; every texture carries provenance + licence status and passes the quality bar.
- **Search (both):** free text with synonym expansion and ranking (exact tag > category > name words), facets/filters, pagination, "similar to"; Postgres full-text first, embeddings only later; library browsing follows the studio plan gate (sound = Saka and up, texture = top plan).
- **Builds now (R1, by the sound agent):** the sound library manifest + taxonomy + search API + a human catalog report for the owner to review. **Next:** the texture library (starter template specs authored as DSL, quality-checked) and a **unified catalog layer** (`lib/cyrus/library`) that serves sounds, textures and later models through one interface, with customer uploads stored as Cyrus-prefixed records; then the browse/search UI inside the studios (design mockups in progress).



### R2 Composition, data packs, import (about 7 days)
### R3 Creatures, full studios, designers (L; after R2 is stable)
- **26.x creature pipeline**: BetterModel managed plugin; RigSpec compiler; 3 archetypes; 5 clips; banshee end to end; hitboxes and attacks; performance budget per server (T).
- **Full Texture and Sound Studios**: layers/undo/palettes/selection/tiling preview/onion skin; waveform, spectrum, layering; reference-image-to-spec via a vision model; asset history with diffs.
- **Gameplay Designers**, one at a time: Custom Item Designer; ability/event graph (typed triggers -> conditions -> actions compiled to validated code, no arbitrary scripts) with a verified component library; then GUI, quests/NPCs, bosses, progression, minigames. Auto-generated Dialog config screens (1.21.7+).
- **Playtest scripts** from spec acceptance criteria (Mineflayer).

### R4 World and reach (L)

# Cyrus studios v2: design notes (mockups, 2026-10-10)

Files: `item-designer.html`, `menu-quest.html` (tabs Menus / Quests), `mod-packs.html`, `import-mod.html`, `datapack-studio.html`. Self-contained, no network. Sources `src/` (v1 kit + `v2.css`/`ext.js`), build `tools/build.py`, shots `tools/run-shots.sh` (node-2, capped) into `shots/` (28 PNGs). Query params pick states; `ctl=0` hides the mockup bar.

## Principles
- **One product.** The shell copies the shipped studio (impl-shots/texture-*): the real portal sidebar and top bar, the Cyrus bar (wordmark, crumbs, context switch, Mod assets, token chip, theme), glass panels with mono eyebrows, the inspector tab anatomy, the conic-rim prompt dock at the bottom of the centre column.
- **One accent.** Violet means selected or primary. Cyan only means "now" (the simulator playhead). Green, amber, red only mean pass, warn, fail/blocking.
- **Typed, never node soup.** Graphs are columns (When, Only if, Do) with nested loop containers; blocks show their config path (`a0.n1`).
- **Caps are budgets.** Every limit is a meter or a counter (`20/64 actions`, `3/16 biomes`, `214/2048 progress chars`), and an overrun shows the validator's own code and message.
- **Honesty.** Real-client gameplay is "not verified" everywhere. "Not run" is never a pass. Sample content is labelled. The one illustrative Test Flight state is bannered as such. The attested scan never says safe.

## Mapping to backend data
| Screen | Data and caps |
|---|---|
| Item Designer | `ItemDesign` v1 (the Void Reaper fixture verbatim). Budget meters = `budgetOf()` ported 1:1 vs `BUDGET` (64/32/8/512/3), nodes 48, depth 3, 16 actions per list. Gate column = the `Ability` protocol (re-entry, cooldown, charges, conditions). Parameters = `params.ts` paths (`items.void_reaper.abilities.void_pull.a0.radius`) with `CAPS` ranges; saving shows "config.yml only, config_version 1→2, 27 Java files unchanged". Structure fields name the one Java file they rebuild. Simulator = `simulate.ts` semantics: charge = held/max, per-owner mark cap with oldest replaced, feedback text on cooldown. Asset chips run `canAsset` (texture top plan, sound Saka+). |
| Menus | `MenuDesign` chest (shop fixture: 6 rows, 28 list slots, 30 config entries, prev/next 48/50). Cost types item / xp_levels / economy; the CostCharger order room → pay → take → give drives "Try it". Checks use real codes (`economy_needs_vault`, `cost_loop`, `arbitrage_loop`, `slot_overlap`). |
| Quests | `QuestDesign` (trial_one/two/three, daily_bread fixtures): requires, branches (max 3), repeat daily, objectives with counts, rewards (max 8), stored-progress size from `progressEntryChars`. Backend is in progress (feature/cyrus-r11, uncommitted). |
| Mod Packs | Inventory (`scanServer`, redacted keys counted), findings with the engine's class/severity/resolution table, server-only findings separated, `notChecked` listed, `nxpack.json` summary (merged pack, `required: false`, changelog), compatibility row (static / boot, `not_run`), dynamic plan (1 combined + differential boots), the unit install steps and backup lifetime. Install off: `CYRUS_MODPACK_INSTALL_REAL`. |
| Import | ImportDemo fixture: ingestion caps, build files read-not-run, attestation + share consent with the text-version ids, SPDX detection, the allowlist (placeholderapi, vault-api), `unsupported: X`, the attested profile's 5 real warnings, revision 0 facts from the node-2 run, token estimate from the reserve table (Saka standard 60–220). Jar = analysis only, dock disabled. |
| Data packs + worldgen | DataPackSpec v1 resource kinds and pack caps, six pinned versions, per-version emitted JSON (attributes + `#rrggbb` from 1.21.11, music list from 1.21.4, carvers map on 1.21.1), the function allowlist and refusals (live "Try a command"), function limits, the template layout spec (palette chars, `.` void, 48³, 32768 blocks, 16 loot containers), the cost heuristic and per-class recommendation, the restart / new-chunks banner. |

## Component inventory (React)
- Shared: `StudioShell` (existing), `DesignerSwitch`, `TargetVersionChip`, `BudgetMeter({label, used, cap})`, `IssueList({issues})`, `QualityPanel` (reuse).
- Item: `ItemHeader`, `AssetRefChip({kind, key, decision})`, `AbilityGraph({ability, selected})` → `TriggerBlock`, `GateChain`, `ActionBlock`, `LoopContainer`; `ParamField({path, value, cap, changed})`, `ParamsPanel`, `PendingEditBar({edits, files, configVersion})`, `DesignSimulator({design, events})`, `DisplayContextPreview` (reuse the shipped In game view), `DesignDock` (parameter-request preview).
- Menu: `SlotGrid({rows, slots, list, page, mode})`, `Slot`, `SlotInspector`, `ClickProtocol({steps})`, `ConfigListTable`. Quest: `QuestChain`, `QuestFlow` → `StepCard`, `ObjectiveRow`, `BranchColumns`, `RewardChips`; `QuestSimulator`.
- Packs: `MemberList`, `InventorySummary`, `FindingCard({finding, onResolve})`, `ManifestSummary`, `CompatRow`, `UnitInstallCard`.
- Import: `UploadKinds`, `IngestChecklist`, `AttestationForm`, `DetectedFacts`, `DependencyRow({state})`, `AttestedScan`, `RevisionZeroCard`.
- Data packs: `ResourceTree`, `VersionStatusRow`, `BiomeForm` (+ one form per kind), `EmittedJson({version})`, `TemplateEditor({layers, palette})`, `IsoPreview`, `FunctionSafety`, `WorldgenCost`, `RestartBanner`.

## Interaction details
- Graph and Parameters edit the same value; selecting a block highlights its settings; old values show struck through.
- Menus: Edit selects slots (numbers on hover); Try it buys with a sample inventory and shows each protocol step; arrows page the list.
- Quests: chain cards select a quest; player events advance the simulator; +24 h re-opens the daily.
- Packs: Apply / Acknowledge / Undo per finding; Install and Test Flight stay disabled while anything blocks.
- Data packs: the target version changes JSON and checks; paint template cells with a palette char; upper layers dim in the preview.
- Narrow (< 760 px): summary plus Approve / Reject on every screen.

## Accessibility
Kit focus rings; status always has text, not colour alone; `role="checkbox"`/`aria-checked`, `aria-required`; MC-coloured names sit on a dark chip in light mode; reduced motion stops the glint and dock rim. Open: keyboard painting for the slot grid and template cells, screen-reader summaries of the graph and the timeline.

## Deliberately excluded
Free-form wiring and code blocks (`run_command` does not exist), the dialogue-menu editor, forms for every resource kind (biome, template and functions are drawn), creatures/RigSpec, vanilla item art, prices, invented test results.

## Open questions for the owner
1. **Item icons.** The mockups use pixel icons drawn here. Production needs a source: our own icon set, or icons rendered from the client's assets (licence check)?
2. Should settings-only edits skip the model and cost 0 tokens (`planDesignEdit` is built, not wired)?
3. Menu and quest designers are still in progress on feature/cyrus-r11. Are dialogue menus and the 8-menu / 16-quest limits the scope you want?
4. Can a Mod Pack install while user-decision warnings are open (today: yes, unless acknowledgement is required)?
5. Third-party members: search Modrinth/Hangar, or paste a link? The download allow-list isn't wired.
6. Worldgen restart: automatic after install, or confirmed by the customer? On uninstall, keep or archive the dimension folders?
7. Are "Try it" and the quest simulator customer-facing, or creator-only?
8. Attestation and share-consent wording: approve the texts shown?

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Inline v2/src/<page>.html + css + js + fonts + images into self-contained mockups in v2/ (no network)."""
import base64, re, os, sys
D = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))); S = os.path.join(D, "src")
PAGES = ["item-designer.html", "menu-quest.html", "mod-packs.html", "import-mod.html", "datapack-studio.html"]
MIME = {".webp": "image/webp", ".png": "image/png", ".svg": "image/svg+xml", ".woff2": "font/woff2"}
cache = {}
def data(rel):
    p = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(S, rel))
    if p not in cache: cache[p] = f"data:{MIME[os.path.splitext(p)[1]]};base64," + base64.b64encode(open(p, "rb").read()).decode()
    return cache[p]
def assets(t): return re.sub(r"\.\./assets/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.(?:webp|png|svg|woff2)", lambda m: data(m.group(0)), t)
for src in (sys.argv[1:] or PAGES):
    if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(S, src)): continue
    h = open(os.path.join(S, src)).read()
    h = re.sub(r'<link rel="stylesheet" href="([^"]+)">', lambda m: "<style>\n" + open(os.path.join(S, m.group(1))).read() + "\n</style>", h)
    h = re.sub(r'<script src="([^"]+)"></script>', lambda m: "<script>\n" + open(os.path.join(S, m.group(1))).read().replace("</script", "<\\/script") + "\n</script>", h)
    h = assets(h)
    assert "../assets" not in h, src
    open(os.path.join(D, src), "w").write(h)
    print(src, round(len(h) / 1024), "KB")

# Cyrus Texture and Sound Studios: design notes (mockups, 2026-10-10)

Files: `texture-studio.html`, `sound-studio.html`, `mod-assets.html`, `locked-states.html` (self-contained; sources `src/`, build `tools/build.py`, shots `shots/`).

## Principles
- **Polish in place, no new look.** Tokens, type and chrome are copied from the v5 handoff (`app/dashboard/cyrus/studio.css`): deep space `#05030b`, glass panels, Inter + Space Grotesk + JetBrains Mono, the TopBar crumbs, the conic-rim prompt dock, the inspector tab anatomy, the handoff's 1.7-stroke icon set. The asset entry is a new **Assets** tab in the existing inspector, over the network map.
- **One accent.** Violet is the only accent. Cyan only means "live": the playhead, the selected layer, the compare splitter. Green, amber and red only mean pass, warn and fail.
- **Truth first.** The mockups run the repo's real code (bundled from `lib/cyrus/textures` and `lib/cyrus/sound`). Quality panels show real `tq-1`/`sq-1` results (the Glock genuinely warns on `palette_size` 49; gunshots warn after peak limiting). Library rows are real manifest metadata. The only stand-in is library *audio* (it stays on the render host), and the page says so.
- **AI never overwrites**: every Cyrus edit is a candidate to compare, apply in part, or reject.
- **Real light mode**: white glass, inked colours; the portal rail stays a dark island, as in the portal.

## Mapping to backend data
| Screen | Data |
|---|---|
| Texture canvas, layers | `TextureSpec` (generated base, locked) + a raster Paint layer on top. Accepting a candidate swaps the spec. The PNG is a build artifact. |
| Palette, ramps | `spec.palette` (max 24, `MAX_PALETTE`). Ramps are UI groupings; "New ramp" generates 5 hue-shifted shades. |
| Style DNA | The prompt's CUSTOM TEXTURES rules (one outline colour, top-left light, 3-5 shade ramps, no noise or gradients, clear background); compliance is measured with the `noise` and `outline` checks. |
| Checks | `textureQuality()`: `transparency`, `palette_size`, `contrast`, `noise`, `outline`, `vanilla_lookalike` (`not_run`). `soundQuality()`: `format`, `true_peak`, `loudness`, `audible`, `silence_ratio`, `dc_offset`, `duration`, plus a subtitle row. |
| Sound events | `SoundSpec`: sets → events (`role`, `category`, required `subtitle`) → 1-4 weighted variants → up to 4 layers (`lib:` / `synth:` / `silence`, with gain, pitch, start, trim, fades) + processing. The key is `nx_<8>:<set>.<event>`. |
| Meters | `measure()` + `ROLE_PROFILE` bands; auto gain and peak limiting come from `renderVariant()`. |
| Pack status | R0/R1 sync states: hosted, delivery off (`CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL` off), unhosted; `required: false`; the Bedrock line from `assetLines`. |
| Locks | `canAsset(plan, kind, op)`, ported 1:1. Only create/edit is gated. The copy is the gate's own `reason` strings and the `downgradeSpecAssets` notice. |
| History | Asset revisions (spec + render + quality per revision). Restoring makes a new revision. |

## Component inventory (React)
- `StudioShell({studio, mod, plan})`: TopBar crumbs, Texture/Sound switch, token chip.
- `PixelCanvas({raster, zoom, grid, mirror, backdrop, tool, selection, compare})`, `ToolRail({tool, mirror, grid, color})`, `CompareBar({mode: split|onion|diff|after})`.
- `LayerList({layers, active, onToggle})`, `EditSteps({steps, at, onJump})`.
- `PaletteStrip({palette, ramps, color, usedCount})`, `RampGenerator({from})`, `StyleDnaStrip({rules, follows})`.
- `LivePreview({raster, mode: hotbar|hand|tile, bg})`.
- `CandidateCard({before, after, changes[], picks, qualityDelta, onAccept, onApplyPart, onApplyInSelection, onReject})`, shared by both studios.
- `QualityPanel({report})`, `CheckRow({id, status, value, limit, message})`.
- `EventList({sets, selected})`, `EventHeader({key, role, category, subtitle, onSubtitle})` (states: valid, missing).
- `VariantTabs({variants, candidate, weights})`, `WaveformEditor({pcm, layer, zoom, playhead, onTrim, onFade, onMove})`, `LayerLane({layer, solo, selected})`, `FxRow({processing})`.
- `LoudnessMeters({measure, role, gainDb, peakLimited})`, `LibraryBrowser({query, group, category, items})`, `SynthPicker({preset, params})`.
- `AssetsTab({mod, pack, textures, soundSets, plan})`, `PackStatusCard({state})`.
- `StudioLock({kind, decision})` (states: locked, plan_unknown, included), `PlanMatrix({plan})`, `DowngradeNotice({denials})`.

## Interaction details
- Texture tools: B, E, G, I, M, L, U; X = mirror, # = grid, +/- = zoom, Ctrl+wheel zooms, Esc clears the selection, Ctrl Z / Ctrl Shift Z undo and redo. Every stroke is one step. Partial apply works per change (checkboxes) or inside the selection.
- Sound: Space plays, L loops. Drag a layer's edges to trim, its top corners to fade, its body to move it. Sliders re-render live. A/B plays V1, then the candidate.
- Quality checks re-run on every edit.
- Narrow: read-only preview, checks, play, approve/reject (approve saves a revision).

## Accessibility
Focus rings everywhere; tools have `aria-pressed` + shortcut hints; subtitle is `aria-required` with inline error; status is never colour alone; AA-tuned v5 inks; reduced motion respected. Open: the canvas and the waveform need keyboard pixel and handle movement (arrow keys + Enter) and screen-reader summaries.

## Deliberately not included
3D model or block preview (the "In hand" view is a flat extrusion), mob-skin UV editing (shown as "later"), animation and `.mcmeta`, reference-image-to-spec, image-model or AI-audio providers, spectrum view and pitch-preserving stretch, Texture Library contents (no source exists yet), prices.

## Open questions for the owner
1. Plan naming: the gate says Free / Katara / Saka / **All models** (Yakko); the handoff says Sokka/Yako. Which spelling is final?
2. Token cost per asset edit: the dock shows no estimate because there is no measured price yet. Should it show one, and when?
3. Should packs be optional on join (current default) or required?
4. Library licence: the bundle licence forbids redistributing the files. Do processed sounds inside customers' packs comply (legal check)?
5. Should the mob-skin row stay visible as "later", or be hidden until it's built?
6. Should mobile approvals be allowed, or should mobile be view-only?
7. Inspector width: Assets needs about 560px versus 480 today. Widen just this tab, or open the studios full-page?

content.thinking:
I don't have three.js available locally, and installing it would need network access, so instead I'm leaning toward writing a small hand-rolled canvas renderer—painter's algorithm with flat shading and textured cuboid faces—similar to the existing preview.ts approach.

For the vehicle mockup, I'll procedurally build a low-poly car (chamfered box body, cylindrical wheels) with flat shading and a livery texture via simple planar UV projection, rendered with the same triangle painter's algorithm. WebGL via headless Chromium/SwiftShader feels riskier than sticking with Canvas2D.

I'm now planning a shared mini 3D engine (camera, orbit controls, cuboid/triangle mesh builders, texel sampling, raycast picking) plus shared CSS layered on kit.css and v2.css, which will support four pages—starting with a viewport-paint page showing a Minecraft gun item model with a model list and layers panel.

For the paint/channel view, I'm deciding to show a PBR channel switcher where only Albedo and Emissive are actually exported for Minecraft, with other channels honestly greyed out as "not used by Minecraft Java." I'll include a view mode switcher (Lit, Albedo, Normal, Roughness, Metallic, AO, Emissive, UV checker, Wireframe) plus a context switcher for in-hand previews (Hotbar, Dropped, First/Third person, Item frame, Head) and a state scrubber for animation poses.

Now I'm sketching the actual layout: a central viewport with a floating tool rail (brush, eraser, fill-face, picker, mirror X), a top strip with asset name, view/channel toggles, and undo/save controls, plus an axis gizmo and palette strip at the bottom. The right side holds the in-game live preview and inspector tabs (Paint/Channels/Checks/History), while the left side lists models, a 2D UV texture map that mirrors brush painting live, and layers. Then I'm moving on to planning the Layer 2 cuboid/bone editor for the banshee creature's rig.

For model-editor.html, I'm designing the RigSpec editor with an outliner tree, 3D viewport with transform gizmos, and an inspector covering cube properties (from/to, size, pivot, rotation, UV box mapping) and bone properties (pivot, tags), plus a bottom timeline with animation clips, tracks, keyframes, a playhead, budget meters, and an AI prompt dock that surfaces edits as review candidates. Now I'm starting on retexture.html, the Layer 3 editor for an imported glTF vehicle livery from FiveM, beginning with the asset info panel on the left.

Now I'm detailing the asset info panel further — legal class badge noting it's game-derived and not redistributed, job lifetime, material slot list, and per-slot channel layers (albedo with base paint/decals/logos, normal, roughness, metallic) with lossless compositing. The center splits into a 3D viewport and a 2D UV island view showing the painted livery, while the right side holds export target pickers for FiveM, RedM, GMod, and other games with status notes on what's built versus planned, alongside a legal notice clarifying only the livery texture ships and the base mesh is never stored or redistributed, plus decal transform controls and a worker job status card.

For the locked page, I'm defining plan-gated states for the Model Studio — view-only orbit with export/install allowed, fail-closed on unknown plans, a maturity flag for experimental formats like Hytale, and a narrow 390px read-only approve view, all driven by query params for state and width. Since the narrow approve view seems to belong mainly to this locked page but could apply across all screens, I'm deciding to build a shared renderNarrow helper in ms.js that shows a rotatable model preview, summary, checks, and approve/reject actions, reused across all four pages with page-specific data to keep things efficient.

For MODEL-STUDIO-PLAN.md, I'm keeping it under 2500 words with tables, and DESIGN-NOTES.md under 800 words. I'm working out the plan-tier gating logic — proposing Model Studio and Layer 3 retexture sit at the top plan tier since they involve writing textures/models, while viewing, orbit, in-hand preview, and install/export stay ungated for anyone with a Cyrus project; Saka would get view-only plus maybe pose preview, keeping the rule consistent that anything writing texture or model requires the top plan, including AI-generated RigSpec models from prompts. I'll present this as an options table and recommend option A, then move on to the Hytale specifics.

For Hytale, I'm flagging unverified details about the .blockymodel format — JSON structure, node hierarchy, shape types (box/quad), UV textureLayout per face, pivot units, the .blockyanim animation format, texture size limits, and the server asset pack manifest — noting these come from my own unverified knowledge and should be labeled U. I'm also sketching the server-side preview render design as two separate lanes: a cuboid lane extending the existing software rasteriser for deterministic, GPU-free PNG output with golden hash tests, and a mesh lane for Layer 3.

For the mesh/PBR lane, I'm planning headless Chromium with Playwright plus three.js on SwiftShader software WebGL, locked to fixed resolution, camera presets, and DPR, with no animation clocks and preserved draw buffers so renders stay reproducible — using toleranced pixel-diff comparisons rather than exact matches since SwiftShader varies across driver versions, and pinning the Chromium build in the worker image. I'm defining the worker as a capped `linux-cpu` job queue with content-addressed outputs keyed by spec/renderer/camera hashes, resource limits via systemd slice, a 60s timeout, and no network access beyond local files.

Now I'm setting performance budgets: 60fps for small scenes, tri/texture caps in the editor with heavier exports reserved for the worker, a GPU memory ceiling, sub-16ms paint latency for 2048 textures, and load-time targets for glb assets with lazy-loaded three.js chunks on the studio route — plus a mobile fallback using read-only orbit preview, capped DPR, and server-rendered turntable PNGs when WebGL isn't available.

I'm starting to think through undo/redo, autosave, and conflict handling, where the client keeps a working spec copy alongside an operation log.

Each edit becomes a single history step reusing the existing History type with structural sharing or inverse commands. Autosave writes a per-user draft row server-side on a timer so reloads restore state without creating real revisions, while explicit saves create a proper revision and asset row guarded by optimistic concurrency that returns a stale-head conflict. For AI edits mid-session, the AI never touches the working copy directly — it produces a candidate diff against a base revision that's only auto-applied if nothing local has changed those same nodes since.

If the human did edit concurrently, I need a three-way merge at node granularity, which means cubes need stable ids. Since RigSpec v1 is a strict schema and can't take new fields without breaking the build service, I'm leaning toward wrapping it in a ModelDoc structure that carries an id map, editor state, and paint data alongside the untouched spec rather than modifying RigSpec itself.

For UV editing, the current auto-layout approach conflicts with manual overrides, so I'd need a RigSpec v2 that adds optional per-cube UV coordinates and a painted skin image, which means a compiler change too. More critically, the painted skin texture is generated from the layout plus a paint layer, so if a cube gets resized and the layout shifts, the paint pixels become misaligned — I need a strategy to invalidate or remap paint data when relayout happens.

The fix is to pin each cube's UV once painted, so resizing only relays that specific cube, with painted texels resampled to fit the new face size and a warning shown — this is worth flagging as a risk. Separately, I'm checking Minecraft's item model rotation constraints (limited angles around a single axis) since that affects how the gun cuboid model can be oriented, though I'm unsure if newer versions relaxed this restriction.

For the item editor, I need the validator to enforce vanilla rotation rules per model version and support explicit per-face UVs in 0-16 space. This means defining a new "ItemCuboidSpec" with elements (from/to bounds extending beyond the normal 16 range), face UVs, rotation constraints, display transforms, and per-state models that each emit a model JSON into the pack — directly solving the "gun not visible in hand" problem by giving it real 3D geometry with proper display transforms shown consistently in the in-hand preview.

Now I'm working through the skin texture packing: computing shelf-packed net dimensions for each cube based on pixel density, then figuring out the exact UV offsets for each of the six box faces (east, north, west, south, up, down) per the compile.ts formula, and making sure each face's texel axes align correctly with its rectangle dimensions in my 3D mapping.

content.thinking:
The car is still cropping on the left because of the narrow horizontal field of view in this portrait viewport — with vertical FOV at 30° and aspect ratio 0.6, horizontal FOV shrinks to about 18°, so I need to push the camera distance out further, maybe around 16, to fit the diagonal car properly.

I'm making distance dynamic based on aspect ratio. The jagged livery stripes are a bigger issue though — they come from flat-shaded triangles with sharp stripe boundaries, and the proper fix would be affine texture mapping per triangle (using canvas clip plus drawImage with a shading overlay), though that's much slower for 18k triangles.

Working out the lighting overlay: for each textured triangle I'd compute a shading factor from the lit color of a mid-grey sample, then multiply-blend black or white at the appropriate alpha to darken or brighten the texture. Deriving the affine transform matrix mapping texture UV coordinates to screen triangle vertices...

Since each triangle uses its own island consistently across all three vertices, the mapping stays coherent. I'm worried about performance though — 18k triangles each doing a save/clip/setTransform/drawImage of a large 1024x768 canvas could get expensive in software rendering, maybe 1-2 seconds total, and only body_paint triangles need this treatment. I should scale back tessellation density to roughly 110x44 (about 9.7k triangles) since the texture mapping itself no longer requires such fine subdivision.

At that count, each frame costs roughly half a second, which is fine for a static view but would make orbit dragging feel laggy. I'm considering falling back to flat shading during drag and only switching to textured rendering once the drag ends, but decide it's simpler to just always use textured rendering. I'll implement this in the 3D render path by checking if the object has a texture function and using the textured path when available.

input.content:
# Cyrus Model Studio: plan (design only, 2026-10-10)

Labels: **V** = I read it in code (cyrus-r2 `lib/cyrus`, cyrus-r13 `assets3d/manifest.ts`, `adapters/asset-profile.ts`, `jobs/asset-jobs.ts`). **U** = unverified. Every quality claim about AI output is **U until a paid eval runs**. Mockups: `*.html` + `shots/` in this folder.

## 1. What exists today (V)
| Piece | Where | Fact that matters here |
|---|---|---|
| RigSpec v1 | `creature/spec.ts` | Zod `strictObject`; bones/cubes/clips; caps 32 bones, 64 cubes, 8 clips, 48 KB; model never writes UVs |
| Compiler | `creature/compile.ts` | box UV `boxFaces` + shelf `layoutSkin` (64/128), deterministic `.bbmodel` (rig-c1) |
| Preview | `creature/preview.ts` | pure software rasteriser, byte-stable PNG |
| Item states | `itemmodel/*` | 8 display contexts, per-category transforms, states; gun transform U in client |
| Texture Studio | `studios/paint.ts`, `editor.ts`, `service.ts` | `TextureDoc` = locked spec + sparse paint layer; `History<T>` 200 steps; save = new revision + asset row, `expectedHeadId` → 409 `stale_head` |
| Gate | `engine-core/asset-gate.ts` | `ASSET_MIN_PLAN.model = "all"`; only create/edit gated; unknown plan fails closed |
| Foundation (r13) | `assets3d/manifest.ts`, `asset-profile.ts`, `asset-jobs.ts` | glTF + sidecar, legal ledger, `libraryEligible`, `WORKER_CLASSES`, in-memory queue + object store (no DB tables yet) |

## 2. Architecture per layer
| Layer | Serves | Canonical data | Human edits | Runtime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 viewport + paint | every model | `ModelDoc` + `TextureDoc` per texture (reused) | paint, fill face, pick, decals | three.js (MIT) client, lazy route chunk |
| L2 cuboid + bone editor | MC creatures (RigSpec), MC 3D items (`ItemCuboidSpec`), Hytale | RigSpec v1.1 / ItemCuboidSpec v1 | cubes, bones, pivots, UV boxes, keys | client ops on the spec; compile server-side |

3. Library: does removal pull the asset from mods already using it?
4. Real-weapon names: hold for review (proposed) or block; allowed in private mods (proposed yes).

| F3 | ItemCuboidSpec v1 + emitter into the pack + states | L | Opus | F2 |
| F4 | Cuboid preview lane on node-2 (jobs, cache, contexts, turntable) | M | Sonnet | F1 |

| L2b | timeline + keys + clip validation | M | Opus | L2a |
| L2c | candidate 3-way merge UI | M | Opus | L2a |
| H1 | `.blockymodel` emitter behind maturity flag + fixtures | M | Sonnet | F2 |
| L3a | glTF import, sidecar, legal class, job retention, channel layers | L | Opus | F1 |
| L3b | UV island view, layer transforms, export picker; mesh preview lane | M | Sonnet | L3a |
| L3c | FiveM YTD packing on the Windows worker | L | Opus | L3a + worker |
| L4a | Blender script worker + look loop + cleanup pipeline + meshBudget | L | Opus | F1, paid eval |

# Cyrus Model Studio v3: design notes (mockups, 2026-10-10)

Files (self-contained, no network): `viewport-paint.html` (a; `?mesh=1` = Layer 4 AI-mesh state), `model-editor.html` (b), `retexture.html` (c), `locked-states.html` (d; `?state=unknown|experimental`), `library.html` (e; `?tab=mine`), `prompt-flow.html` (f). Sources `src/` (v2 kit + `ms.css`, `ms.js`, `m3d.js`, `models.js`), build `tools/build.py`, shots `tools/run-shots.sh` (node-2, capped slice) → `shots/` (28 PNGs: dark, light and 390 px narrow for each). `ctl=0` hides the mockup bar.

## Principles
- **Same product as v2.** Portal sidebar and top bar, Cyrus bar with a Texture / Sound / **Model** switch, glass panels with mono eyebrows, inspector tabs, conic-rim prompt dock, narrow read-only approve view.
- **Real geometry, not pictures.** `m3d.js` is a small deterministic canvas renderer standing in for three.js: orbit, picking, channel views, wireframe, affine-mapped textures. Painting on the gun really writes texels in the 64 × 64 UV texture; the timeline scrubs a real pose; layer toggles on the livery rebuild every channel.
- **One accent.** Violet = selected/primary. Cyan = "now" (timeline playhead) only. Green/amber/red = pass/warn/fail. One exception: gizmo and axis triad use muted X/Y/Z red/green/blue, the 3D convention people expect.
- **Profile-aware truth.** Channels a game cannot ship are disabled with the reason (Minecraft Java item: albedo only). Delivery status per export target (FiveM "planned": the Windows worker is not built). Hytale shows its unverified format list. "Not run" is never a pass.
- **Legal class is visible.** Game-derived templates carry an amber badge, "kept for this session only, never shared", and ship delta-only. The library shows provenance, attribution and every check.

## Screens → data
| Screen | Data |
|---|---|
| a Paint | `ItemCuboidSpec` draft of `glock_9mm` (9 elements, 22.5° grip), `TextureDoc` paint layer (51 px "worn edge"), `ItemModelSpec` contexts (6) + states (idle/aim/reload; reload slides the slide back), checks incl. `grip_in_hand` |
| a `?mesh=1` | L4 output: LOD0-3 vs `meshBudget` (sample numbers), materials as lossless channel layers, cleanup checks, provenance `ai-mesh` |
| b Editor | RigSpec `banshee` (8 bones, 12 cubes, 5 clips), live budgets vs real caps, box-UV net on the 128 sheet with Auto-pack / Pinned, candidate bar with "1 overlap" (3-way merge) |
| c Retexture | glTF template stand-in (8,788 tris, 7 slots), body_paint layers with albedo/rough/metal values, UV island view, export picker with delivery status, policy row from the adapter legal block |
| d Locked | `canAsset(plan, "model", "edit")` strings verbatim; plan matrix with the proposed rows marked; Hytale maturity flag |
| e Library | automatic contribution: states pending checks / in the library / held for review / removed / not shared; lib-1 filters; `libraryEligible` exclusions |
| f Prompt flow | "AK-47 with fire stickers" → L2 + L1 route → ItemCuboidSpec + decal layer → deterministic render (sha) + look check → hand fixes as revisions → library "held" (real-weapon name) |

## Component inventory (React)
`ModelViewport({doc, profile, channel, overlays, tool, onPick})`, `ChannelSwitch({profile})` (inline or dropdown when narrow), `ToolRail`, `GizmoLayer({mode, pivot, space, snap})`, `InGamePreview({itemModel, context, state})`, `UvTexturePanel({texture, highlight})`, `Outliner({bones, selection, candidate})`, `BudgetPanel({stats, caps})`, `TransformFields`, `UvBoxField({layout, pinned})`, `Timeline({clips, tracks, t})`, `CandidateBar({candidate, overlaps})`, `MaterialSlots`, `ChannelLayerList`, `UvIslandView({islands, channel})`, `ExportTargets({profiles})`, `LegalClassBadge`, `PolicyCard`, `PolyBudget({lods, budget})`, `StudioLock` (reuse) + `PlanMatrix` (reuse, new rows), `LibraryGrid`, `LibraryDetail`, `LibraryFilterRows`, `ContributionTable`, `LibraryStateBadge`, `PromptFlow`.

## Interaction details
- Left drag on the model = tool (paint/select); right drag or empty space = orbit; wheel = zoom. B/E/G/I paint tools; Q/W/E/R/P select/move/rotate/resize/pivot; X mirror; Ctrl Z / Ctrl Shift Z.
- Hover shows `element · face · texel` and outlines that face in the UV panel.
- Every stroke, drag, key or accepted candidate is one undo step; drafts autosave; "Save revision" is explicit.
- Narrow: turntable, what changed, checks, Approve / Reject; locked plans get view-only with no approve.

## Honesty notes
Sample content is labelled; poly counts, look-check scores and filter results are illustrative. The mockup renderer is not the production renderer (three.js) and the lantern proxy is lower-poly than its LOD1 readout. Gun display transforms, element rotation rules per version, everything Hytale, RAGE normal convention and every AI quality claim are unverified.

## Questions for the owner
1. **Plan:** Model Studio at All models (matches today's gate), or paint-only for Saka?
2. **Library access:** you said "usable by anyone"; the gate today treats "Use in project" as asset creation (All models for models). Open it to every plan, or keep browse-open / use-gated?
3. **Library removals:** when an asset is removed after a report, do mods already using it keep it?
4. **Real-weapon names** (AK-47, Glock): hold for review in the library (proposed) and allow freely in private mods?
5. **Terms of Service:** the automatic licence grant needs a lawyer's wording; also AI-output copyright per region. Who drafts it?
6. **Uploads gap:** `libraryEligible` lets user uploads through (`source: "user"`). Confirm they must be excluded (I think yes) so the code gets an `uploaded` source.
7. **L4 spend:** budget for the paid quality eval, a GPU worker, and Meshy/Tripo trials?
8. **Hytale:** build the emitter now behind the experimental flag, or wait for a real client to test against?
9. **Retexture templates:** session-only (proposed) is safest but means re-attaching the file each time. Acceptable?
10. Gizmo axis colours as the one accent exception: OK?

It covers layers 1–4 (4 = AI mesh, which you added), data model, autosave and revisions, merging AI edits mid-session, preview render on node-2, Hytale risks, community library, tests, sized tasks with Sonnet/Opus split, owner decisions and risks.
- **Mockups:** 6 self-contained pages that draw real 3D (painting writes real pixels): paint (`?mesh=1` shows layer 4), cuboid/bone editor, car livery retexture, locked states (Saka, unknown plan, Hytale experimental), the automatic library, and the "AK-47 with fire stickers" prompt flow.
- **Screenshots:** 28 in `shots/`, dark, light and phone width, rendered on node-2. I checked them and fixed what looked cramped.
- **Notes:** DESIGN-NOTES.md.

**Gap in r13 code:** `libraryEligible` lets user uploads into the library (`source: "user"`), and a livery painted on a game-derived template would also get in.

**Owner questions:** plan placement (I propose All models); whether "usable by anyone" in the library includes "Use in project" (today's gate locks it); what happens to mods using a removed asset; real-weapon names (hold, not block); a lawyer for the licence wording in the Terms of Service; budget for the paid AI-mesh quality test and a GPU worker; Hytale timing.

**Unverified:** all AI quality claims, everything Hytale, gun hand positions, item rotation rules, and FiveM delivery.
